content.title: Does Homelander Kill Ryan? 'The Boys' Season 5, Ep 3 Ending Explained
content.text: Published April 15, 2026, 12:16 p.m. ET 0 seconds of 30 secondsVolume 0%Ad 1 of 2. 00:2200:0700:30 The Boys Season 5, Episode 3 gives Homelander’s son Ryan (Cameron Crovetti) the showdown he tragically needed. Butcher (Karl Urban) has always seen Homelander (Antony Starr) as a threat to human existence, but Ryan has long been at the center of their feud. Season 4 saw Butcher try to recruit Ryan to The Boys’ efforts in trying to end Homelander, with disastrous results: Ryan, feeling trapped, ended up killing Grace and going back on the run. By the time Ryan returns in Season 5, Episode 3, it’s clear that his character is stuck between two extremes in Homelander and Butcher: If he sticks by Homelander’s side, he can also become a god. But Butcher puts it in no uncertain terms when Ryan confesses that he’s struggling to avoid hurting others. “Without Supes, the world is a better, safer place,” he tells Ryan over a beer. Butcher seemingly convinces Ryan to help him end Homelander once and for all. But it would require Ryan to die, too, which is a massive responsibility to put on any teenager’s shoulders. It shows just how far Butcher has gone in his quest to end Homelander as he convinces that their deaths, as Supes, will bring about justice to the world. That quest may have just gotten harder, too. The Boys learned at the start of the episode that Soldier Boy survived the virus because he was created with V1, an early version of Compound V that hasn’t been in circulation since the 1950s. Despite being Soldier Boy’s son, Homelander doesn’t have V1 in his system, but he will stop at nothing to get his hands on it if it means he can live forever. But did Homelander kill his son? Keep reading to see what you might have missed from The Boys Season 5, Ep 3 ending. The Boys Season 5, Ep 3 Ending Explained: What happened to Ryan in The Boys? Photo: Prime Video The Boys Season 5, Ep. 3 ends with Ryan calling Homelander to meet one more time. Homelander, ever the narcissist, is convinced Ryan called him to ask for forgiveness. Homelander’s delusions of grandeur have hit a fever pitch as he promises (or rather, threatens) he’s going to live forever, since he sent his goons to hunt down Stan Edgar in the hopes of finding the V1 that will make him immune to the virus and allow him to live forever. “I put too much pressure on you to fill my boots and I realize now that was impossible,” he tells Ryan. “I am going to live forever now, I’ll realize my own legacy and you, you’re off the hook.” Ryan then shocks Homelander by asking him if he was conceived by rape. Homelander denies it, but Ryan accuses him of lying, using a line that Homelander likes to deploy often: “Your heart is racing.” Ryan begins attacking Homelander, but it’s clear that he’s no match for the Supe. Just as he begins to draw blood, Homelander slams Ryan down and starts to relentlessly punch him. “My sweet, sweet boy,” Homelander says as he gets one last look at Ryan’s face before he pummels him almost to death. The Boys does not let the viewer escape the brutality of the scene, either. The show offers a closeup at Ryan’s tragically battered face as he stares at his father raising his fist to land what sounds like a fatal blow. Later, Homelander is in his apartment at Vought with blood on his hands. Homelander, who is obsessed with legacy, and being a father and being loved by his own father, just killed his own son. Or did he? Just as Stan Edgar arrives in Homelander’s apartment, possibly to offer him a path to immortality, Butcher arrives to find Ryan beaten and bruised. After a painfully long moment, Ryan is seen struggling to breathe, but he’s very much still alive. This could mean Butcher still has one last ace up his sleeve. New episodes of The Boys air Wednesdays on Prime Video.
